research_notes: The close record should not claim precise active-work seconds unless measured; an estimate should be labeled as such.
Elapsed wall time can be exact from captured timestamps.
Work-unit count is a useful corroborating measure but not a substitute for active-work duration.
Tool-call latency is operationally real even when it is not model reasoning time.
For maximum-safe-runtime classification, elapsed wall time remains decisive.
For throughput optimization, later analysis can decompose elapsed time by activity type if useful.
